Retrieve Employees Recent Schedule. Employee Recent Schedules endpoint returns by default, the last three shifts for an employee looking back seven days. Updating the offset will allow you to reach back N of shifts in the previous seven days. This endpoint includes an option to stack shifts, summarizing shift punch in/out and punch source across posts. Punch Source options are PSTT, PSTT reconcile, and Team Time. If IsStackedShifts is true, we'll combine contiguous shifts based on work date and job number.

This could return a large result set. Filtering and Paging is always recommended when no Employee Number is provided.

Add Job. The POST Job API allows new Job records to be created in WinTeam if all required fields are passed and no duplicate Job Numbers exist. Get Employee Deductions. Returns all non-garnishment deductions assigned to an employee; garnishment and admin-fee deductions are excluded and managed separately; returns an empty array (not 404) when the employee exists but has no deductions.

Create Employee Deduction. Creates a single deduction record for an employee. Optional fields (deductionTypeId, basis, amount, paycheckDescription, printOrder, glNumber, vendorNumber, recurringLimit) default to values from the deduction template when omitted. startDate and endDate are required for ECP integration compliance. Garnishment and admin-fee deductions are not supported in phase 1.

Update Employee Deduction. Partially updates an existing employee deduction using JSON Patch (RFC 6902). startDate and endDate remain required for ECP integration compliance. Garnishment and admin-fee deductions are not supported in phase 1. Basis cannot be changed from a flat/recurring type (1–3) to WageBased (4) or DeductionBased (5); delete and re-add the record instead.

Delete Employee Deduction. Hard-deletes a single employee deduction record. Child garnishment records are cascade-deleted by the database trigger. Matches WinTeam desktop delete rules. Returns 422 when the deduction is referenced by an unprinted paycheck.
